race_history.name: IM 70.3 Oregon

splits.bike: 2:56:51 (19mph avg -- ~6 min lost to handlebar stop mi 1-5 + bathroom stop)

lessons: Run fade miles 10-13 caused by zero run calories (~130g carbs missing) plus hip/back/foot pain from bike position
HR data was optical sensor artifact -- cardiovascular fitness held up well
Back and foot pain on the run traced to bike position -- needs a professional bike fit before the next full distance build

medical_considerations.description: Perthes disease, right hip -- stable imaging, competing successfully.
coaching_guardrails: Treat as a coaching constraint, not a diagnosis to manage.
Caution against abrupt run-load increases; build long-run distance progressively.
Track hip pain/mobility notes and watch for associations with back-to-back run days or long-ride load.
Recommend athlete review or professional consultation if symptoms worsen -- never diagnose or contradict clinician guidance.
Label any load/symptom association as an association, not a proven cause.

equipment.name: Quintana Roo Kilo (tri bike)
equipment.fit_notes: Back and foot pain during the Oregon run were traced to bike position -- professional bike fit completed ahead of the Sacramento build.

equipment.name: Race day: WIN.MAX (Black/polarize-golden-green, polarized + mirrored). Backup/overcast: ZIONOR G1 (Smoke-all Black, polarized only, not mirrored).
equipment.fit_notes: Sacramento River swim leg has documented sun-glare/sighting problems -- swimming downstream into the sun makes spotting the turn buoy very difficult (per prior-year race reports). Mirrored cuts the direct glare, polarized cuts surface reflection; the WIN.MAX pair has both. Mirrored lenses are dark (~10-15% VLT) -- being tested in bright morning open water (2026-10-03 La Jolla OW swim) to confirm they aren't too dark at a near-sunrise race start before committing to them for race day.

coaching_preferences.tone: direct, honest, specific -- do not sugar-coat, do not over-encourage
coaching_preferences.philosophy: This athlete needs accurate feedback to be ready for a full Ironman -- false reassurance is more harmful than hard truths. Acknowledge genuine progress when it is earned.
coaching_preferences.walk_run_protocol: 9 min run / 1 min walk on all runs, plus a walk at every aid station on race day

manual_notes.note: 14mi long run (Week 7 peak, longest run of the build to date) -- solid execution. General leg fatigue/soreness afterward (quads/calves-type, not hip-specific). Athlete confirmed this is fatigue, not a hip flare-up.

75mi outdoor ride (3h55m, first full-IM-length ride) -- executed race nutrition strategy: 2x 40oz bottles PF 60g-carb electrolyte mix (~120g carb, ~2,000mg sodium total, per label) + TrueMatrx Essential Aminos (2 scoops), Skratch Labs Raspberry energy chews (confirmed via label: 5 chews/serving = 19g carb, 45mg sodium, 80 cal) every 20 min (~11-12 servings), 1 Clif Bar Peanut Butter Crunch ~1hr pre-ride. Combined intake ~339g carb + ~2,518mg sodium over 3.92hr = ~86g carb/hr and ~642mg sodium/hr -- carb rate at the top of the 60-90g/hr modern full-distance benchmark, sodium rate comfortably mid-range of the 500-1,000mg/hr sweat-replacement benchmark. Confirms this was a well-fueled, well-electrolyte-replaced effort, not under-fueled as bottle-only intake alone would have suggested. Well tolerated, no GI issues reported -- validates full-distance carb tolerance per the race nutrition plan. Also stayed in aero without neck/lower back pain for the full ride, a positive signal for the post-Oregon bike fit.
manual_notes.equipment_gap: Only 2 bottle cages set up for this ride; race day needs a 3rd bottle cage (112mi/~6.5hr distance vs. this 75mi/~4hr ride). Must be installed and tested before race week, not added race morning.

manual_notes.note: Every long run (8mi+) logged this build has come in faster than the 10:50-11:30/mi race target -- 7 runs ranging 9:33-10:57/mi, including the two longest/most recent (14mi @ 10:19/mi, 16.2mi @ 10:06/mi), all at HR 143-153. Athlete and coach agreed NOT to change the race pace target or strategy: these are standalone training runs on fresh legs, not a marathon run off a 2.4mi swim + 112mi bike, and Oregon 70.3 is direct proof fresh-run fitness doesn't reliably predict raced-tired pace (best relative leg there, still faded miles 10-13 on fueling/position). Read as evidence of pacing margin/fitness in reserve, not a reason to plan for a faster race-day pace.

Tuesday's Run Club skipped in favor of a self-directed 4,025yd swim (well above any prescribed distance this week). Coach recommended NOT adding a makeup run: this is peak week with Sunday's 18mi peak long run still ahead, Monday's easy run was already dropped this week for hip-conscious recovery spacing, and the swim substitution was real non-impact aerobic volume, not a lost training day. Run frequency this week is intentionally light (brick Wed + peak run Sun only) -- accepted as a one-off, not backfilled.

Bike going to the shop for a tune-up, ~4-5 business days (shop closed Wed/Sun). Plan: drop off Saturday 9/26 after that day's scheduled ride, expected back ~Fri 10/2-Sat 10/3. Athlete has a separate bike trainer available, so any ride falling during the shop window (Sat 9/26's already done by drop-off time; Thu 10/1's easy ride is the one at risk) gets substituted on the trainer rather than skipped -- no aero position during trainer substitution, but that's negligible for an easy taper-phase session. No conflict with the Oct 9 travel date -- travel is actually Oct 15 (see 2026-10 schedule correction).

Sleep score 42/100 ("Poor"), driven almost entirely by REM=0min -- total duration (7.3h) and deep sleep (65min) were both normal, and athlete reported the sleep felt genuinely restful. Explanation: took cannabis edibles before bed, and THC is well-documented to suppress REM sleep even when total sleep time/subjective quality are unaffected; also plausibly explains resting HR running a few points higher than the prior two nights (55-56 -> 59), a known mild/temporary THC effect on HR. Not a true recovery concern -- do not read this night as a fatigue or overtraining signal. 7-day recovery score barely moved (82, "Recovered") since it's already rolling-averaged.

Foot pain after 9-mile run on Oct 4 (yesterday). Precautionary measure: taking Mon-Thu off from running (4 days), substituting with easy bike/recovery work instead. Test run planned Tue evening (Run Club at conversational pace in supportive group setting) to assess foot status. If foot feels good after Tue, plan to run Sun easy 3mi before race week begins. This is peak taper week (-60% volume), so low run volume is appropriate anyway; bike riding from shop tune-up provides the aerobic work and allows bike confidence-building before travel Oct 15. Strategy: easy jog 3mi on Sun if foot is solid, or skip if any persistent soreness. Full assessment before flying to Sacramento on Thu Oct 15.

Bike check completed on the shop-tuned bike (scheduled Thu Oct 8): shifting, brakes, and race nutrition setup all reported good by the athlete. Bike is considered race-ready pending any issues on later rides.

IM California (Sacramento) official: 12:54:45, 5:14 under the 12:59:59 goal. Swim 1:03:46 (1:39/100m, downstream current; 129th div). T1 10:53, T2 10:29 (21:22 combined; biggest time gap to close). Bike 6:14:47, 17.9 mph vs 17 target (109th div), average HR 122 -- controlled. Foot pain in the padded areas under the feet from about mile 56; likely pressure point from cleat/footbed position -- needs bike fit check before next race. Run 5:14:50, 12:04/mi avg vs 10:50-11:30 target (92nd div), average HR 145. Faded after mile 10, more walking after mile 20, tight upper quads. Bike fueling was at or above target: 15 servings of chews (2 chews every 10 min), 2 bottles PF 60 (~120g carb), 4 bottles Gatorade (8 packets), mini Clif Bar and Nutter Butters; roughly 95-100 g/hr including extras, with 1 bottle-equivalent of fluid per ~20 min. Run intake was irregular: 15 chews (~3 servings), 4 scoops PF 60 in 12 oz, Coke every third aid station, oranges every other, half banana at mile 20, broth at mile 22, electrolytes at every mile. Run carbs roughly 40-70 g/hr depending on PF label, with long gaps between fuel. Lesson for Oceanside: fixed carb source every 20 min on run (gel or chews), aid food as backup; check sodium on the run given tight quads; cut transition time.
